study.title: Blessed is the man who fears the LORD
study.intro: Psalm 112 is the twin of Psalm 111. Both are Hebrew acrostics, with each half-line starting with the next letter of the alphabet. Psalm 111 praised the works and character of God, and Psalm 112 shows how those same qualities begin to appear in the person who fears Him. Such a person is generous, steady, unafraid of bad news and remembered for their goodness.
study.context: Psalm 112 repeats phrases from Psalm 111 on purpose. 'His righteousness endures forever' is said of God in 111:3 and of the God-fearing person in 112:3 and 112:9. 'Gracious and compassionate' describes God in 111:4 and the upright in 112:4. The message is that people grow to resemble the God they revere. Paul quotes verse 9 in 2 Corinthians 9:9 when he encourages generous giving.
study.peopleNote: No author or individual is named. The psalm describes a typical God-fearing person, not one historical figure. Paul later applies verse 9 to the generous giving of the Corinthian church.

verses.title: Delight in His commands
verses.heading: The man who fears the LORD
verses.meaning: 'Hallelujah! Blessed is the man who fears the LORD, who greatly delights in His commandments.' Psalm 111 ended by saying the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, and Psalm 112 picks up exactly there. The blessed person does not obey grudgingly. They take great delight in what God asks. Reverence and joy go together: honoring God is the start of a glad life, not a gloomy one.
verses.context: The first word of 112 continues the last thought of 111. Psalm 1:1-2 also calls the person blessed whose delight is in the law of the LORD, so this psalm stands in a long line of 'blessed' sayings.
explore: Fears the LORD
Deep reverence and trust toward God that shapes choices, rather than terror that drives a person away.
Greatly delights
Finds real pleasure in, enjoys and looks forward to, not merely tolerates or puts up with.
verses.reflect: Which of God's commands do you find easiest to delight in, and which feels hardest right now?
verses.alt: A villager in a head cloth reading a scroll in morning light.

verses.title: A blessed generation
verses.heading: The generation of the upright
verses.meaning: 'His descendants will be mighty in the land; the generation of the upright will be blessed.' The good effects of a God-fearing life reach beyond one person. Children and grandchildren benefit from the example, the prayers and the reputation they inherit. The psalm speaks in general terms, as wisdom literature does: it describes the usual direction of things, not a guarantee that every family will be spared every hardship.
verses.context: Proverbs 20:7 says the children of the righteous are blessed after him. Like Proverbs, this psalm states a general pattern. Other Scripture, such as Job and Psalm 73, honestly admits times when the righteous suffer.
explore: Descendants
Literally 'seed': the children and later generations who come after a person.
Mighty in the land
Strong, respected and well established among the community where they live.
verses.reflect: What kind of example or legacy would you most like to hand on to those who come after you?
verses.alt: Three generations of a family working together in a vineyard.

verses.title: Riches and lasting goodness
verses.heading: His righteousness endures forever
verses.meaning: 'Wealth and riches are in his house, and his righteousness endures forever.' The phrase 'his righteousness endures forever' was used of God in Psalm 111:3, and now it is used of a person. That is the heart of these twin psalms. Those who fear God come to share something of His character. Whatever material blessing they have, their goodness is the thing that truly lasts.
verses.context: Psalm 111:3 says of God, 'His righteousness endures forever.' Repeating it here shows the upright reflecting God. Jesus taught that treasure in heaven lasts when earthly treasure fades (Matthew 6:19-20).
explore: Wealth and riches
Material goods and household provision, seen in the Old Testament as a gift from God to be used well.
Righteousness
Right living and right relationships, including fair dealing and generosity toward others.
verses.reflect: What in your life do you hope will still matter long after possessions are gone?
verses.alt: A simple stone home with full storage jars and an open door.

verses.title: Light in the dark
verses.heading: Light dawns for the upright
verses.meaning: 'Light dawns in the darkness for the upright—for the gracious, compassionate, and righteous.' Upright people still face dark times, but they do not stay in darkness forever. Light rises for them like morning. Again the words echo Psalm 111:4, where God is 'gracious and compassionate.' People who show God's kindness to others find His light breaking into their own hard nights.
verses.context: Isaiah 58:10 promises that when people pour themselves out for the hungry, their light will rise in the darkness. John 1:5 says the light shines in the darkness and the darkness has not overcome it.
explore: Dawns
Rises gradually like the sun at morning, slowly replacing the dark.
Gracious and compassionate
Kind, merciful and moved by others' needs; words first used of God Himself in Exodus 34:6.
verses.reflect: Where do you need light to dawn in a dark place right now?
verses.alt: Sunrise breaking over dark hills above a sleeping village.

verses.title: Generous and just
verses.heading: It is well with the generous
verses.meaning: 'It is well with the man who is generous and lends freely, whose affairs are guided by justice.' The God-fearing person handles money and business with an open hand and a fair heart. Lending freely meant helping neighbors in need without exploiting them through harsh interest. Generosity and justice belong together; kindness without fairness, or fairness without kindness, falls short of God's way.
verses.context: The Law told Israel to lend to poor neighbors without charging interest (Exodus 22:25; Deuteronomy 15:7-8). Jesus also said, 'Give to the one who asks you' (Matthew 5:42).
explore: Lends freely
Helps a neighbor in need with a loan, given willingly and without taking advantage of them.
Guided by justice
Conducted with fairness and honesty, so that everyone in the deal is treated rightly.
verses.reflect: Is there a way you could be both more generous and more fair in how you handle money this month?
verses.alt: A farmer handing a sack of grain to a neighbor at a gate.

verses.title: Never shaken
verses.heading: Remembered forever
verses.meaning: 'Surely he will never be shaken; the righteous man will be remembered forever.' The upright person has deep roots. Storms come, but they are not toppled at the foundation. And their goodness leaves a mark: they are remembered with gratitude, and above all they are remembered by God, who never forgets those who trust Him.
verses.context: Psalm 15:5 ends, 'He who does these things will never be shaken.' Proverbs 10:7 says the memory of the righteous is a blessing, while the name of the wicked rots.
explore: Shaken
Toppled or moved from a secure place, like a building whose foundation gives way.
Remembered
Kept in mind with honor by people and, more importantly, held in mind by God.
verses.reflect: Who do you remember with gratitude because of the good they did?
verses.alt: An old olive tree standing firm while wind bends the grass.

verses.title: No fear of bad news
verses.heading: His heart is steadfast
verses.meaning: 'He does not fear bad news; his heart is steadfast, trusting in the LORD.' This is one of the most practical promises in the psalm. Bad news will still come, but it does not rule the heart. The reason is not toughness or denial. It is trust: a heart fixed on the LORD stays steady when reports, diagnoses or headlines are frightening.
verses.context: Psalm 57:7 says, 'My heart is steadfast, O God.' Isaiah 26:3 promises perfect peace to the one whose mind is fixed on God because he trusts in Him.
explore: Bad news
Frightening reports or messages, such as word of danger, loss or illness.
Steadfast
Firm, settled and established, not swaying back and forth.
verses.reflect: What news are you afraid of hearing, and how could you place it in God's hands today?
verses.alt: A villager calmly listening as a runner arrives with a message.

verses.title: An assured heart
verses.heading: Until he looks in triumph
verses.meaning: 'His heart is assured; he does not fear, until he looks in triumph on his foes.' Verse 8 repeats and deepens verse 7. The heart is not only steady for a moment but upheld over time, until the trouble has passed. The righteous do not have to win their own battles by anxious scheming; they wait with confidence for God to set things right.
verses.context: Psalm 118:6-7 similarly says, 'The LORD is on my side; I will not be afraid... I will look in triumph on those who hate me.' The triumph is God's vindication, not personal revenge.
explore: Assured
Supported and held up, as something is propped so that it will not fall.
Looks in triumph
Sees the trouble overcome and the threat ended through God's help.
verses.reflect: What long-running struggle do you need God to steady your heart through, not just for today?
verses.alt: A shepherd resting calmly by a fold as storm clouds move away.

verses.title: Gifts to the poor
verses.heading: His horn lifted high
verses.meaning: 'He has scattered abroad his gifts to the poor; his righteousness endures forever; his horn will be lifted high in honor.' Generosity is pictured like a farmer scattering seed widely. The giver does not hoard. Paul quotes this verse in 2 Corinthians 9:9 to encourage cheerful giving. The one who lifts others up is the one God lifts up with honor.
verses.context: In 2 Corinthians 9:6-9 Paul uses this verse while urging generous giving, reminding believers that God loves a cheerful giver and supplies seed to the sower.
explore: Scattered abroad
Given out widely and freely, like seed flung across a field rather than kept in a barn.
Horn
A picture of strength and dignity taken from a strong animal's horn; a raised horn means honor.
verses.reflect: Where could you 'scatter' a gift to someone in need this week?
verses.alt: A sower scattering seed across a plowed field at dawn.

verses.title: The wicked waste away
verses.heading: The desires of the wicked will perish
verses.meaning: 'The wicked man will see and be grieved; he will gnash his teeth and waste away; the desires of the wicked will perish.' The psalm ends with a contrast. The wicked watch the upright flourish and are filled with bitter envy. Their own hopes, built apart from God, come to nothing. Psalm 1 ends the same way: the way of the righteous stands, and the way of the wicked perishes.
verses.context: Like Psalm 1:6, this ending sets the two paths side by side. Gnashing of teeth is a picture of rage and frustration, used also by Jesus in Matthew 8:12.
explore: Gnash his teeth
Grind the teeth together in anger, envy or despair.
Desires
Hopes and cravings; the plans a person sets their heart on achieving.
verses.reflect: What desires in your heart would last if they were built on God rather than on yourself?
verses.alt: Chaff blowing away from a threshing floor in the wind.
